title: The FSD reads the ACE views directly, while Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read them and gives S9 no cell to P1
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 37 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json); Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 (R-PREC, DP table, W-MAP, R9) DP-05
section: A1.1 constraints; A1.4 preconditions; VR-S9-003-1, VR-S9-005-1, VR-S9-007-1, VR-S9-008-1 and VR-S9-013-1 (freshness)
description: The FSD constraint says source data is read only from the ACE database through the SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, landed by ACE ingestion, and A1.4 makes every data product the module reads carry today's business date. Five validation rules read freshness from v_ace_batch_status. Architecture v5 slide 37 changes the position to the views read only by rwb-source-data, slide 45 answers who reads ACE data with rwb-source-data alone, and the slide 13 connection matrix gives the S9 Partner row exactly two cells: R to P5 Document and R to Outside. The Ownership Map records no view as S9's. The read path of every automatic step of this module is therefore undefined in the FSD.
evidence: FSD S9 A1.1 constraints and A1.4 preconditions; VR-S9-003-1, VR-S9-005-1, VR-S9-007-1, VR-S9-008-1, VR-S9-013-1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 matrix row 'S9 Partner' (R to P5, R to Outside only), slide 37, slide 45; Ownership Map Services and endpoints: no S9 view row; Template and Rules DP-05
owner_role: Solution architect with the P1 owner
proposed: Read every fact this module does not own through a contract: case, party and queue facts from rwb-case, and the freshness of each data product from rwb-source-data. Add the missing S9 cells to the matrix, or confirm that the five freshness rules are answered by a contract response rather than a view.

title: The FSD matches the agency recovery and the fee in this module, including ALS and GL, while v5 gives payment and proceeds to rwb-payment and the matrix gives S9 no cell to P8
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 17, 20 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json) endpoints; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 NFR and release sections
section: A2.7 Match a recovery and calculate the agency fee; A2.9 Approve partner fees; REQ-S9-004
description: FSD A2.7 names ALS and GL as integration points and states that the module matches money recovered by an agency to the case and works out the fee due; A2.9 approves the fee claim. Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-partner the items panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees and scorecards, and slide 17 gives its OUT only the schema, topic rwb.partner.events.v1 and a REST link to Document. Payment and proceeds matching, the posting to ALS and the general ledger, and the fees are rwb-payment's (slide 41, wave 2), and the slide 13 matrix gives the S9 row no cell to P8, to P2 or to Outside for a payment call. Who calculates the fee, who pays it and who matches the money is therefore split across two services with no stated boundary.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.7 integration points 'ALS and GL, Partner portal'; A2.9 steps; REQ-S9-004; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 (S9 IN and OUT lines), slide 20 (rwb-payment), slide 41 (both service rows), slide 13 matrix row 'S9 Partner'; Ownership Map: no S9 payment endpoint and no S9 payment event
owner_role: Solution architect with the P8 owner
proposed: This service calculates the fee from the contracted schedule and the recorded result and holds the approved claim; the money is matched and paid by rwb-payment, and the result is read back through a contract. Confirm the path and add the S9 cell to P8.

title: The Ownership Map and the physical schema give three tables, while the service catalogue says the schema holds results, fees and scorecards as well
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json) tables; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 partner, partner_instruction, partner_user; Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql
section: Service contract, rwb-partner OUT DB line
description: Architecture v5 slide 41 states that rwb-partner owns 'panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees, scorecards', and slide 17 repeats it as the schema content. The Ownership Map Tables sheet holds exactly three rows for S9 (partner, partner_user, partner_instruction), the Logical Data Model holds the same three tables with DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-016 and DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217, and the physical schema creates the same three. The scorecard result, the fee claim and its approval, the review, the conduct sample and the field visit therefore have no table, no field list and no key in the register every DB story is written from.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 (DB line 'rwb_partner: panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees, scorecards'), slide 41 (same six items); Ownership Map tables: partner, partner_user, partner_instruction only; LDM v8 the same three tables; Physical Schema v6.sql the same three CREATE TABLE statements
owner_role: Data architect
proposed: Name the scorecard, fee-claim, review, conduct-sample and field-visit tables with the DB story, and keep partner, partner_user and partner_instruction as they are.

title: partner_instruction.case_id is a cross-schema foreign key to recovery_case, while ADR-014 requires a business key and no foreign key out of the schema
source: Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 DF-PRT-009 and the relationship list; Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6.sql partner_instruction; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 (R-PREC, DP table, W-MAP, R9) DP-01
section: A2.1, A2.4, A2.6, A2.9, A2.10, A2.11, A2.12, A2.14 and A2.15 field catalog; section 8.1
description: The Logical Data Model types partner_instruction.case_id as CROSS_REF uuid with FK recovery_case, the relationship list shows partner_instruction to recovery_case as N:1 and mandatory, and the physical schema creates case_id uuid NOT NULL with no constraint to another schema. Architecture v5 slide 29 gives each service its own schema and login with no cross-schema access, and ADR-014 and DP-01 forbid a foreign key that leaves the schema. The FSD field catalog repeats partner_instruction.case_id with the meaning 'The recovery_case this record belongs to' in nine features.
evidence: LDM v8 DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 and the relationship row 'partner_instruction | case_id | recovery_case | N:1 | Yes'; Physical Schema v6.sql CREATE TABLE partner_instruction; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 29; Template and Rules DP-01 and DP-02
owner_role: Data architect with the platform DB owner
proposed: Keep case_id as a varchar(255) business key with no foreign key, as every other service does, and enforce the link at the contract.

title: The field catalog repeats the same eight partner columns in nine features and names no field for the scorecard, the fee claim, the review, the conduct sample or the field visit
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1 to A2.15 field catalogs; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-070 and BR-071
description: Ten of the fifteen features carry a field catalog, and every one of the ten lists the same eight columns: six partner columns and partner_instruction.case_id and partner_instruction.partner_id. No feature lists a scorecard result, a fee claim, a review point or action, a conduct sample, a breach, a field visit, a photograph or a bill, although BR-070 and BR-071 require all of them. The other five features (A2.3, A2.5, A2.7, A2.8, A2.13) carry no field catalog at all.
owner_role: Business analyst, S9
proposed: Treat the eight columns as the partner and instruction entity, and write the remaining field lists with the story that first needs them.

title: No rule row covers allocation by measured return, scoring, review, fee approval, conduct sampling or the field app
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rule sets RES, SET, DIL, GUA, LIT, DIS, DS, WO, DEV and UNI; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 25; Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.3 and A2.8 to A2.15
description: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 holds 448 rules in ten route sets (RES, SET, DIL, GUA, LIT, DIS, DS, WO, DEV and UNI) and none of them is a partner route set. The Temporal and Drools Design names R-UNI-25 to R-UNI-29 and R-UNI-45 for the chase, the recall, the exit, the conflict, the insolvency, the conduct breach and the re-selection, plus R-LIT-24 to R-LIT-29 and R-WO-30 to R-WO-35 for the instructions other modules issue. The allocation on measured return (A2.3, A2.4), the monthly score, the fee approval (A2.9), the review (A2.10), the conduct sample (A2.13), the extra-cost approval (A2.14) and the field capture (A2.15) therefore have no rule row, no rule ID and no message.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4: ten rule sets and no PRM set; R-UNI-25 (chase then recall), R-UNI-26 (panel exit), R-UNI-27 (conflict), R-UNI-28 (insolvency), R-UNI-29 (conduct breach), R-UNI-45 (re-selection), R-WO-30 to R-WO-35, R-LIT-24 to R-LIT-29 only; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 25 (S9 Drools decides: conduct breach suspends allocation, insolvency stops fees)
legacy_ref: RWB-S9-E6029-APP to RWB-S9-E6035-APP, RWB-S9-E7011-APP to RWB-S9-E7018-APP
owner_role: Center of excellence analyst with P7
proposed: Author the partner rule set from FSD A2.3, A2.4 and A2.8 to A2.15, govern it in rwb-decision and evaluate it in this service with the embedded Drools kit.

title: The job map has no rwb-partner job, while the monthly scorecard and the conduct sample need a schedule
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44 and the job map; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json) jobs; Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.8 and A2.13
section: A2.8 Score partners monthly; A2.13 Check partner conduct
description: The Architecture v5 job map holds JOB-01 to JOB-22 and the Ownership Map gives none of them to S9; JOB-16 is the write-off scan on rwb-writeoff and JOB-05 covers durable timers for all services. proposed: Run the monthly scorecard and the conduct sample as Temporal Schedules in rwb-partner through the workflow kit, and add the two rows to the job map.

title: Every FSD acceptance criterion in this module is the same generic statement, and no feature has an alternate flow or a background event
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.4 to A2.15.4; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 (R-PREC, DP table, W-MAP, R9) R7.3
description: Fifteen main success flows each read 'The data and rules it needs are in place | The user acts | The result is recorded with its rule version', and each carries the story note 'Written one epic ahead'. Every alternate-flow table holds the single row 'None | No alternate path' and every system background event table holds 'None | No background event'. The only specific criteria are the two exception rows per feature: the role without the right refused with MSG-P4-002, and the decision log store unavailable with MSG-P7-003. The step-specific behaviour of the fifteen features is therefore not stated in any acceptance criterion.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.1.4.1 to A2.15.4.4: fifteen identical main success rows, fifteen 'None' alternate tables, fifteen 'None' background tables, and AC-EXC-S9-001-01 to AC-EXC-S9-015-02 as the only specific criteria
legacy_ref: RWB-S9-E6029-APP to RWB-S9-E6035-APP, RWB-S9-E7011-APP to RWB-S9-E7018-APP
owner_role: Business analyst, S9
proposed: Read each FSD criterion as the feature's main success statement, carry the two exception rows as they stand, and write the step-specific criteria with the story.

source: _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json (stats and legacy); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 7.3; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 sections 8 and 10.3; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 (R-PREC, DP table, W-MAP, R9) R5.6

title: Epic 4 and Epic 5 need partner instructions in wave 3, while rwb-partner is created in wave 4
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 7.3 and Q-019; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 sections 8, 10.2 and 10.3; Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Screens (PRT-02, PRT-03 first in E4); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 18
section: Release plan; dependencies
description: The BRD 7.3 table names RWB-SVC-S9 as a capability owner for E4 (route decision, guarantees and auction) and for E5 (litigation and enforcement), and gives the service wave 4 against business epic waves of 3. E5 releases law firms through the partner portal at 31 March 2027 (tentative) and E4 releases auction rounds at 28 February 2027 (tentative), while the program 10.2 table creates rwb-partner in wave 4 with the release of 30 April 2027 (tentative). BRD Q-019 asks whether the partner instruction capability is in E4 or in E6 and is not answered in the sources.
evidence: BRD E38 section 7.3 (E4 and E5 rows with S9 wave 4 and business epic wave 3), Q-019, CG-B-REQ-BRD-E38-19; Program v5 section 8 (E4 28 Feb 2027, E5 31 Mar 2027, E6 30 Apr 2027, all tentative), section 10.2 and 10.3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (S4 and S5 rows: T E to S9), slide 18 (Partner instruction for law firms, vendors, agencies in S4, S5, S9); FSD S9 Screens (PRT-02 and PRT-03 first in E4)

owner_role: Solution architect with the S4 and S5 owners
proposed: Publish InstructionWorkflow, EV-20 and EV-21 as a contract ahead of wave 4, so rwb-litigation and rwb-asset build against the fake in wave 3 and the instruction works the day this service lands.

title: The FSD names Power BI as an integration point, and the data lake it reads was removed
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.8.2; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 21 and 37; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 (R-PREC, DP table, W-MAP, R9) DP-17
section: A2.8 Score partners monthly; REQ-S9-007
description: FSD A2.8 lists 'Partner portal, Power BI' as its integration points. Architecture v5 removes the data lake, the daily copy and the data lake interfaces, and replaces them with a read model in rwb-reporting built from events; DP-17 states that a story needing lake data is a gap. The scorecard itself is built in this service, so only the publication of the monthly result to the review forum is affected.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.8.2 integration points; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 21 and 37 (no data lake; rwb-reporting read model); Template and Rules DP-17; ADR-018
owner_role: Solution architect with the P9 owner
proposed: Publish the scorecard and the review outcome as events and the decision record, and let rwb-reporting serve the forum and the dashboard; no Power BI extract leaves this service.

source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.14.2; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 20 and 41; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-071; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json)
section: A2.14 Manage extra costs and services on an asset; FEAT-AST-07
description: FSD A2.14 lists 'Partner portal, AMIS' as its integration points, its prerequisite is FEAT-AST-07 (the asset module), and BR-071 requires the additional partner costs on a held asset to be recorded and approved. title: The three staff screens and the four partner portal screens have no owner, and their first appearance precedes the service wave
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Screens; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json) endpoints; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 (R-PREC, DP table, W-MAP, R9) DP-19

title: The partner portal base is /partner/v1/* in the FSD and in Architecture v5, while the naming rule is /api/recovery/<short>/v1
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 17 and 41; Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.2 to A2.15.2 integration points; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 (R-PREC, DP table, W-MAP, R9) R4 and DP-13; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json) endpoints

title: The FSD names no capability area and two of the four lists the module needs
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.3.2 to A2.15.3.2 and A2.1.4.3; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-INSTRUCTION and LOV-INSTR-STATUS

Neither list nor the capability area appears in the FSD, and the Ownership Map records none of them, so the permission and the two list values the build needs are unstated in the functional baseline.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.1.3.2 to A2.15.3.2 (LOV-PARTNER-TYPE, LOV-PANEL only), A2.1.4.3 'the capability area of the screen'; AC-EXC-S9-001-01 to AC-EXC-S9-015-02; LDM v8 LOV-CAPABILITY row PARTNER_PORTAL, LOV-INSTRUCTION, LOV-INSTR-STATUS, DF-PRT-011 and DF-PRT-014; Ownership Map: no LOV rows
owner_role: Security administrator with the business analyst, S9
proposed: Use capability area PARTNER_PORTAL and the two instruction lists as the Logical Data Model holds them, and confirm the role matrix with P4 before the first screen is built.

title: REQ-S9-002 (one named owner per partner type) is served by no feature, and no field holds the owner
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.16 and section 11; Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Requirements served and A1.2; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-060
section: Requirements served, REQ-S9-002; A1.2 feature overview
description: The program requirement REQ-S9-002 states that each partner type has one named owner and is Must for E6, and BR-060 lists it among its eight source requirements. owner_role: Business analyst, S9 with the partner and agency manager
proposed: Record one owner role per partner type as a versioned panel row read at run time, and refuse an allocation where the type has no owner role.

title: Partner identity is a table in rwb_partner while the requirement that governs it is delivered by rwb-access
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 11 trace; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 7.3 and REQ-ACA-012; Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Existing capability check; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 partner_user
section: A1.1 constraints; PRT-01 and PRT-02; section 9
description: The program 11 table delivers REQ-ACA-012 (partner users reach the Workbench only through the external gateway, with multi-factor authentication, scoped to their own cases) with RWB-SVC-P4 rwb-access in wave 1. The Ownership Map and the Logical Data Model give the partner_user table, the partner identity binding and the partner role to S9, and its ruling records that P4 keeps the internal role model only. The FSD's existing capability check lists 'role and permission matrix' as REUSE from ACE's common module and names no owner for the external identity, and the split plan gives the story RWB-S9-E2019-APP to S9.
evidence: Program v5 section 11 (REQ-ACA-012 to RWB-SVC-P4, wave 1); BRD E38 REQ-ACA-012 and RWB-E2-019; Ownership Map ruling on partner_user (ASM-A6-tables-6); LDM v8 partner_user DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217; FSD S9 Existing capability check
owner_role: Security administrator with the P4 and S9 owners
proposed: P4 keeps the internal role model and the gateway enforces the external identity; S9 holds the partner_user binding that scopes a partner user to one firm and one partner role.

title: No retention class is stated for partner, partner_instruction or partner_user
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 6.5 and DL26; Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A1.1
section: Section 8.1 retention column; A2.12 End a partner contract
description: NFR-028, NFR-030, NFR-031 and NFR-075 leave the retention period of every record class open under DL26, and the FSD states no retention class for the partner, the instruction or the partner user. A2.12 ends a partner contract and recalls the work, and no source states how long the closed partner, its instructions and its results are kept. The retention column of this document therefore states the class and not a period.
evidence: Program v5 section 6.5 (NFR-028, NFR-030, NFR-031, NFR-075, all open under DL26); Non Functional Specification v3; LDM v8 (no retention column); FSD S9 A1.1 and A2.12
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer
proposed: Carry the Workbench record class and leave the period open until DL26 answers, as every other service does.

title: One placement rule has two owners: S7 owns the treatment decision and the recovery, and the FSD gives the placement itself to S9
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-059 and section 8.4; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.14 and 5.16; Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.6; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-30 to R-WO-35
section: A2.6 Place a charged-off account with an agency; A2.7
description: BR-059 sources its placement requirement from REQ-S7-006 and REQ-S7-007 and lists FEAT-PRM-06 among its features, while FEAT-PRM-06 is an S9 feature in the FSD. Program 5.14 gives REQ-S7-006 (post charge-off treatment by rule, including placement with an agency) and REQ-S7-007 (recoveries after charge-off matched, with income and agency fees) to S7, and 5.16 gives S9 no placement requirement of its own. R-WO-30 to R-WO-35 carry the placement, the capacity hold, the result, the underperformance recall and the replacement under the write-off route set. Two services therefore claim one rule and one state change.
evidence: BRD E38 BR-059 (sources REQ-S7-006, REQ-S7-007, FEAT-PRM-06, RWB-E6-034) and section 8.4; Program v5 5.14 (REQ-S7-006, REQ-S7-007) and 5.16 (no placement requirement); FSD S9 A2.6 and Requirements served; R-WO-30 to R-WO-35
owner_role: Solution architect with the S7 owner
proposed: S7 decides the treatment and posts the recovery after charge-off; S9 issues and tracks the placement instruction and holds the panel, the terms and the recall.

title: The module has no message of its own, and no Thai wording is stated for any of its messages
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.3.1 to A2.15.3.1; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 DL10 and NFR-059; Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3
section: A2.1.3.1, A2.2.3.1 and the other validation-rule tables
description: Every validation-rule table in the FSD uses one of four messages: MSG-GEN-001 (required field empty), MSG-P1-001 (a data product is stale), MSG-P4-002 (a role without the right) and MSG-P7-003 (the decision cannot be recorded). No MSG-S9-nnn exists, so the refusal, the capacity hold, the fee difference, the recall reason and the conduct breach have no message ID or wording. NFR-059 requires every label, validation message and error message in Thai and English, and DL10 leaves the Thai wording with the business lead under Legal and Compliance approval.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.1.3.1 to A2.15.3.1 (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 only); Program v5 section 9 DL10 and section 6.10 NFR-059; Error and Message Standard
owner_role: Business analyst, S9 with Legal counsel and Compliance
proposed: Take the wording from the Error and Message Standard for the reused messages and author the module's own messages with the story, in Thai and English, before the wave-4 release.

title: The scorecard measures, weights and thresholds are not in the sources, which repeat one metric for all fifteen features
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.1 to A2.15.1; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 KPI-011 and BR-070; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.16
section: A2.8 Score partners monthly; A2.3 Allocate work by measured return
description: Every one of the fifteen features carries the same intent table: the metric 'Placements by scorecard', the target '100 percent', measured 'Decision log and Workbench records', reviewed Monthly. REQ-S9-003 requires allocation by measured return against a scorecard and BR-070 requires a monthly score, but no source states the measures, the weights, the thresholds or the panel capacity rule. KPI-011 reports the override rate and sets no target.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.1.1 to A2.15.1 (identical metric, target, measurement and review in every feature); Program v5 section 5.16 REQ-S9-003; BRD E38 BR-070 and KPI-011
owner_role: Partner and agency manager with the center of excellence analyst
proposed: Hold the measures, the weights, the thresholds and the capacity rule as versioned data rows and agree the initial set with the scorecard story.

title: The fee approval needs the approval workflow on rwb-decision, and the matrix gives S9 no cell to P7
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.9; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 15 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json) workflows
section: A2.9 Approve partner fees; REQ-S9-004; BR-070
description: FSD A2.9 checks the fee claim against the schedule and the result and approves it, and BR-070 requires the fee to be checked and approved. Architecture v5 gives the approval workflow, the maker-checker route, the delegation limits and the decision record to rwb-decision, and the slide 13 connection matrix gives the S9 Partner row no cell to P7 at all, while the rows of S2, S3, S5, S6 and S7 each show T to P7 for their DoA approvals. The note under the matrix says every service writes DecisionRecorded to rwb-decision, which covers the record but not the approval route. Who routes the fee approval, and by which call type, is therefore unstated for this module.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.9 and its steps; BRD E38 BR-070; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (S9 row: R to P5 and R to Outside only; S2, S3, S5, S6 and S7 rows: T to P7), slide 15 (rwb-decision ApprovalWorkflow and the DoA limits), slide 41 (rwb-decision owns approvals), and the matrix note 'DecisionRecorded to rwb-decision'
owner_role: Solution architect with the P7 owner
proposed: Route the fee approval through the approval workflow on rwb-decision by Temporal, as the other route services do for their DoA approvals, and add the S9 cell to P7 in the matrix.

title: Partner performance, conduct and complaint data must reach the review forum, and rwb-reporting subscribes to no partner event
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.8 and Requirements served; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-070, REQ-S9-007, KPI-011; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 and slide 43
section: A2.8 Score partners monthly; REQ-S9-007; section 9
description: REQ-S9-007 requires partner performance, conduct and complaint data to be reported to the partner review forum and BR-070 repeats it. Architecture v5 makes reporting a read model in rwb-reporting built from events (ADR-018, DP-17), yet the slide 13 connection matrix gives the P9 Reporting row no cell to S9, so rwb-reporting subscribes to no topic of this service, and slide 43 gives EV-20 and EV-21 the consumers partner portal, rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-case only. The measure KPI-011 (override rate) is read from the decision record, which does reach rwb-reporting, but the scorecard, the review outcome and the conduct result have no published fact and no subscriber.
evidence: Program v5 section 5.16 REQ-S9-007; BRD E38 BR-070 and KPI-011; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (P9 row: no S9 cell; P9 subscribes to P3, S2, S3, S6, S7 and P6 only), slide 43 (EV-20 and EV-21 consumer lists), slide 21 and 37 (no data lake; reporting read model)
owner_role: Solution architect with the P9 owner
proposed: Publish the scorecard, the review outcome and the conduct result as events on rwb.partner.events.v1 and add S9 to the P9 subscription, or confirm that the report is produced inside this service for the forum.

title: The contractual notice on a missed target has no path: the FSD gives the notice to this module and the matrix gives S9 no cell to rwb-comms
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S9 Partner management v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.11; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 17 and 19; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 (22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json)
section: A2.11 Issue a notice on a missed target; REQ-S9-005
description: FSD A2.11 requires the contractual notice to be sent when a partner misses its targets, with the cure period started; BR-070 and R-UNI-25 repeat the notice in the recall path. Architecture v5 gives notice content, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery to rwb-comms, and gives rwb-litigation a Temporal and event path to it (slide 13 S4 row: T and E to P6). The slide 13 S9 Partner row carries no cell to P6 and no event cell at all, so this service neither calls the comms service nor subscribes to its delivery event. The notice content and its proof of delivery therefore have no owner on the path this service is allowed to use.
evidence: FSD S9 A2.11 and its steps; BRD E38 BR-070; R-UNI-25; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (S9 row: R to P5 and R to Outside only; S4 row: T and E to P6), slide 17 (rwb-comms IN and OUT), slide 19 (rwb-litigation child notice), slide 41
owner_role: Solution architect with the P6 owner
proposed: Issue the contractual notice through rwb-comms by Temporal and subscribe to its delivery event, as rwb-litigation does, and add the two S9 cells to P6 in the matrix.
